reconcile.connective: Tyndale's commentary distinguishes the lights' calendrical and doxological role in Genesis from the predictive reading astrology gives them.

discrepancy.connective: Steve Wells argues Genesis 1:14 puts the stars there 'for signs' — exactly what astrologers read — while Leviticus and Deuteronomy call that abomination.

skeptic.name: Steve Wells
skeptic.attribution: Steve Wells, Skeptic's Annotated Bible (1999), contra/astrology.html

excerpts.excerpt_text: They do not predict the future, as Israel’s neighbors believed (see Jer 10:2).
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly denies that Genesis's 'signs' function is predictive/astrological, distinguishing it from the divination practice banned in Lev 19:26 / Deut 18:10-12.

pd_work.resource: Keil & Delitzsch, Biblical Commentary on the Old Testament (1861-75)
pd_work.author: Keil & Delitzsch
pd_work.note: K&D's note on Genesis 1:14 treats the 'astrological and chronological utility' of the heavenly lights directly, distinguishing portents/prognostication of weather and events from the divinatory abuse condemned in the Law; confirmed John Haley's Examination of the Alleged Discrepancies of the Bible (1874) does not treat this passage (full-text search for 'astrolog' returned zero hits).
